precepts.text: It grieved them exceedingly that there was come a man to seek the welfare of the children of Israel. They do not like it when we speak up for our people.
precepts.point: The squeaky wheel gets the oil. We will complain, judge, bring out the records, and beg the Lord until he kills our enemies and sets us up, like the widow before the unjust judge. Our enemies want us silent, locked away with our mouths zipped, calling us troublemakers; yes, we are causing trouble, because you are not supposed to be over us. Nehemiah 2:10 shows they grieve when a man comes to seek the welfare of the children of Israel.

note.label: The Image of Dysfunction or the Image of God Which One Are You?

precepts.why:
The Lord has set watchmen upon the walls of Jerusalem “which shall never hold their peace day nor night”. Watchmen pay attention to the condition of the people and to the enemy coming to destroy the people. “ye that make mention of the Lord, keep not silence, And give him no rest, till he establish, and till he make Jerusalem a praise in the earth.”

Nehemiah shows how the enemy takes it when Israel speaks up: “When Sanballat the Horonite, and Tobiah the servant, the Ammonite, heard of it, it grieved them exceedingly that there was come a man to seek the welfare of the children of Israel.” They do not like it when we speak up for our people.

That is why our enemies want us silent, locked away with the key thrown away and our mouths zipped. They call us troublemakers. Yes, we are causing trouble, because you are not supposed to be over us. They want a quiet slave.

The squeaky wheel gets the oil. Quiet people are ignored, and noisy people force others to take action. So we will complain, judge, bring out the records and tell it like it is, and we will beg the Lord and give him no rest, like the widow before the unjust judge, until he kills our enemies and sets Jerusalem up on high.

precepts.text: Fear is nothing else but a betraying of the succours which reason offereth. Frolic produces an image of comfort that is false: the athlete making millions running up and down the court thinks he has made it, but the real soul knows he is still a slave. Kaepernick caught the fever and stood up, and they made an example of him; his teammates know he was right and pretend to be fine. That pretence is fear. We cannot drown out the squeaking of our wretched condition with frolic, drugs, alcohol, or music, dancing slaves made to look whole while the spirit rots.
precepts.point: The squeaky wheel gets the oil. We will complain, judge, bring out the records, and beg the Lord until he kills our enemies and sets us up, like the widow before the unjust judge. Our enemies want us silent, locked away with our mouths zipped, calling us troublemakers; yes, we are causing trouble, because you are not supposed to be over us. Nehemiah 2:10 shows they grieve when a man comes to seek the welfare of the children of Israel.

note.label: The Image of Dysfunction or the Image of God Which One Are You?

precepts.why:
“For fear is nothing else but a betraying of the succours which reason offereth.” Succours means comforts. Fear is a betraying comfort.

We are encouraged to be sports figures, entertainers and dancers, to frolic: to play, jump and move about in a happy, lively, carefree way, and never think about anything serious, because then we become a danger. Frolic produces an image of comfort that is false. The athlete makes millions running up and down the court and thinks he has made it, but the real soul of him knows he is still a slave. Keeping us in the silly mode makes us consumers, not people who run our own banks and medical centers.

Kaepernick caught the fever. He looked at what was happening to his people while he was up there throwing the ball, got serious and stood up, and you saw how they dealt with him. His teammates know he did the right thing, but they have to pretend they are all right. That pretending is the fear: they stay in that mess and never stand up to be men, lying to themselves that they are comfortable being clowns.

So the watchmen of Isaiah 62 cannot hold their peace. We cannot drown out the horrible squeaking of our wretched condition, the psychological traumas we live through, with frolic, drugs, alcohol or music. We cannot be dancing slaves made to look whole while inside there is a spiritual rot we can no longer afford. We must stand up and be real men and women, keep not silence, and give the Lord no rest.

precepts.text: And give him no rest, till he establish, and till he make Jerusalem a praise in the earth.
precepts.point: For there are set thrones of judgment, the thrones of the house of David. Pray for the peace of Jerusalem: they shall prosper that love thee. Some of y'all busy praying for Haiti, praying for Puerto Rico, praying for Mexico, praying for America. But the Bible said pray for Jerusalem. Remember, Jerusalem's a people before it's a place. We are Jerusalem. Pray for us. We're not supposed to be praying, stop the war over there; no, we got to move them out of our land so that we can go back home.

note.label: Raising Up the Tabernacle of David That Fell

precepts.why:
David says, “Pray for the peace of Jerusalem: they shall prosper that love thee.” Some of y'all are busy praying for Haiti, praying for Puerto Rico, praying for Mexico, praying for America. But the Bible said pray for Jerusalem.

Isaiah says how to pray for it: “And give him no rest, till he establish, and till he make Jerusalem a praise in the earth.” Give the Lord no rest until he establishes Jerusalem and makes it a praise in the earth.

Remember, Jerusalem is a people before it is a place. We are Jerusalem; pray for us. We are not supposed to be praying, stop the war over there. No: they have to be moved out of our land so that we can go back home. That is the peace of Jerusalem, and that is the prayer that gives God no rest until it is done.

precepts.text: Give him no rest, till he establish, and till he make Jerusalem a praise in the earth. That is what we do. But if we really wanted it, there is no way we would entertain sin under our noses while telling the Lord to hurry up. You might get slain.
precepts.point: The sea is the navy and the battleships; the trees burn when the fire comes; it is the same scene as 2 Esdras 13:5, the multitude gathered from the four winds to subdue the man from the sea. The nations will try to fight Christ to keep us in slavery, and he is coming to destroy every one of them, and us too if we are not right.

note.label: The Vantage Point of the Elders: the Fathers Have Spoken

precepts.why:
The four angels hold the four winds “that the wind should not blow on the earth, nor on the sea, nor on any tree”, and the cry goes out, “Hurt not the earth, neither the sea, nor the trees, till we have sealed the servants of our God in their foreheads.” So the question always comes: when are we getting out of here? By right, we want to get out. We pray every day, Lord, bring the destruction so we can leave.

Isaiah 62:7 is that prayer: “And give him no rest, till he establish, and till he make Jerusalem a praise in the earth.” That is what we are doing. We are not to give the Lord rest until he delivers us, establishes us and makes Jerusalem a praise in the earth.

But the question is, do we really want it? If we really wanted it, there would be no way we would be entertaining sin, no way we would allow evil right up under our noses while telling the Lord to hurry up. You mess around and you get slain.

The Lord has his timetable, and we are not on that level. You only see your own point of view; you do not have the Lord’s vantage point, looking at everything on this planet coming into the synchronicity he is waiting for. The angels are holding back whole armies until the sealing is finished, perhaps until that one last brother wakes up. You cannot push him. What you are responsible for is your own spirit and your own shenanigans. Get yourself right, and he will take care of the rest.

precepts.text: Israel's last end is a crown of glory and a royal diadem, the land no more termed forsaken but married, and the Most High rejoicing over her as a bridegroom over the bride.
precepts.point: Let me die the death of the righteous, and let my last end be like his. The last end of Israel is a crown of glory in the hand of the Lord: the land married, double for our shame, everlasting joy, and a seed acknowledged among the Gentiles as the seed which the Lord hath blessed. That is why we cannot wait for those days.

note.label: Numbers 23: How Shall I Curse, Whom God Hath Not Cursed?

precepts.why:
“Let me die the death of the righteous, and let my last end be like his!” What is the last end of Israel? “Thou shalt also be a crown of glory in the hand of the Lord, and a royal diadem in the hand of thy God.”

“Thou shalt no more be termed Forsaken; neither shall thy land any more be termed Desolate: but thou shalt be called Hephzi–bah, and thy land Beulah: for the Lord delighteth in thee, and thy land shall be married.” The land no more termed forsaken but married, and the Most High rejoicing over her: “as the bridegroom rejoiceth over the bride, so shall thy God rejoice over thee.”

That is the last end Balaam wished for himself, a crown of glory in the hand of the Lord, and it is why we cannot wait for those days.

precepts.text: As a young man marrieth a virgin so shall thy sons marry thee, and as the bridegroom rejoiceth over the bride so shall thy God rejoice over thee; the gospel is about us being joined back to Christ.
precepts.point: The line is gone out through all the earth, the gospel going out to the end of the world, and in them he set a tabernacle for the sun.

note.label: Psalm 19: The Perfect Law That Converts the Soul

precepts.why:
“Their line is gone out through all the earth, and their words to the end of the world.” That is the gospel going out to the end of the world. And what is the gospel about? “For as a young man marrieth a virgin, so shall thy sons marry thee: and as the bridegroom rejoiceth over the bride, so shall thy God rejoice over thee.”

As a young man marries a virgin, so shall thy sons marry thee; as the bridegroom rejoices over the bride, so shall thy God rejoice over thee. The gospel is about us being joined back to Christ, the bridegroom rejoicing over his bride.
